newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Yieh Loong group denies fraud.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Yieh Loong group denies fraud.

text.p: Taiwan's Yieh Loong steelmaking group on Tuesday adamantly denied any involvement in a scandal in which officials allege that counterfeit invoices were used by some 40 firms to carry out financial fraud.
"We strongly deny any charges saying our group was involved in the scandal," vice-president Chang Shui-wang of Yieh Loong member firm Yieh Phui told Reuters by telephone.
"Absolutely, we have not used any fake invoices," he said, speaking on behalf of his firm and fellow steel group members Yieh Loong and Yieh Hsing.

A spokeswoman for the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday confirmed that the watchdog agency was focusing on the three listed firms for possible involvement in the scheme as part of a wider inquiry also involving police and prosecutors.
"The commission will urge related government offices to continue investigating the case, and we will demand the three listed firms to explain more details," the spokeswoman said.
"All three listed firms in the Yieh Loong steel group have denied involvement in the scandal," she added.
No other listed firms were believed to be among the 40 companies suspected of using the fake invoices.
Other agencies were investigating the unlisted firms, the spokeswoman said.
Few details were available about the group suspected of masterminding the scheme, which prosecutors said was run under an unlisted shell company, the commission spokeswoman said.

But authorities believed the organisation made counterfeit invoices worth over T$10 billion that were then fraudulently used by some 40 companies to obtain bank loans or help their listings, she said.
The three Yieh Loong firms are engaged in production of a variety of specialised steel products.
In 1995, Yieh Phui made a net profit of T$1.3 billion on sales of T$10.6 billion, Chang said. ($1 = T$27.4)
